title: Edmonton Trivia Night

questions.q: Which river winds through Edmonton's long green river valley?
Galaxyland amusement park and the World Waterpark are both inside which Edmonton shopping centre?
Between 1984 and 1990, which NHL team won the Stanley Cup five times?
In 1988 the Oilers traded Wayne Gretzky to which team?
In 2021 Edmonton's CFL team took on which new name?
The original Fort Edmonton was a trading post of which fur-trade company?
Which Back to the Future star was born in Edmonton in 1961?
How many glass pyramids make up the Muttart Conservatory?
Which steel bridge, opened in 1913, carries a heritage streetcar across the river valley in summer?
Thanks to the Fringe, the Folk Music Festival and many more, Edmonton is known by which nickname?

notes: The North Saskatchewan River flows through the centre of Edmonton; see North Saskatchewan River and Edmonton River Valley (Wikipedia).
Galaxyland and World Waterpark are attractions inside West Edmonton Mall; see West Edmonton Mall (Wikipedia) or wem.ca.
Oilers won the Cup in 1984, 1985, 1987, 1988 and 1990; see Edmonton Oilers (Wikipedia) or NHL.com.
Gretzky traded to Los Angeles on 9 August 1988 ('The Trade'); see Wayne Gretzky trade (Wikipedia).
Formerly the Edmonton Eskimos; renamed the Edmonton Elks in June 2021; see Edmonton Elks (Wikipedia).
Fort Edmonton was a Hudson's Bay Company post founded in 1795; see Fort Edmonton (Wikipedia) or Fort Edmonton Park.
Michael J. Fox born 9 June 1961 in Edmonton, Alberta; see Michael J. Fox (Wikipedia).
Muttart Conservatory's four glass pyramids house its display gardens; see Muttart Conservatory (Wikipedia) or the City of Edmonton's site.
High Level Bridge opened 1913; the Edmonton Radial Railway Society runs a streetcar over it in summer; see High Level Bridge (Edmonton) on Wikipedia.
Edmonton's 'Festival City' nickname, from its many festivals including the Edmonton International Fringe Festival; see Edmonton (Wikipedia, Nicknames) or Explore Edmonton.
